slides.lookFor: Students enter with Chromebooks closed until the privacy directions and opening-question model are stated.
slides.pivot: Keep this cover up while the teacher demo account and Completion Standards report are ready.

slides.lookFor: Students are seated and ready for an individual assessment block.
slides.pivot: Move students to lower-distraction seats before launching Xello.

texts:
Today’s Lesson
Model the scale
Answer 39 questions
Open Find out why
Reflect privately

Chromebook
ClassLink + Xello
One assigned reflection page
No screenshots of results

Discussion

One activity you like
One task you avoid
What might those answers suggest about work?
slides.lookFor: Students can name the assessment, Find out why, and private reflection as three separate actions.
slides.pivot: Do not show a real student profile; keep the demo account ready.

slides.lookFor: One liked activity, one avoided task, and a tentative connection—not a permanent label.
slides.pivot: Allow fictional or course-only examples; no hobby or family disclosure is required.

texts:
Your answers change the order of career matches.
A surprising or weak match is still useful evidence.
You can change, learn, and investigate before deciding anything.
slides.lookFor: Students understand that the result is a starting point, not a grade or destiny.
slides.pivot: Ask for a silent thumbs-sideways if a student has ever changed an interest.

texts:
Matchmaker may begin with a goal question.

Answer it as part of Matchmaker, then continue. It is not a separate assignment.
slides.lookFor: Students answer the opening question privately and continue into Matchmaker.
slides.pivot: If several accounts do not continue, move those students to the teacher-sample reflection route and record one catch-up list.

texts: Read each statement • Use the full scale • Ask for a read-aloud when a word is unclear. Quiet individual work: the goal is an honest pattern, not the fastest finish.
slides.lookFor: First lap: all ready students are in Matchmaker and reading rather than rapid-clicking.
slides.pivot: If one third stalls on vocabulary, pause for one sample read-aloud and restart the quiet block.
slides.trim: Do not trim the 28-minute assessment runway; trim optional video or whole-group discussion.

texts:
WORK BLOCK 2
Finish the first 39 questions.
Review the career matches that appear.
Open one career.
Do not move to another About Me assessment.

DONE WHEN
39 questions complete
One career open
Find out why selected
slides.lookFor: Second lap: students use varied responses; finished students are reviewing matches, not starting another quiz.
slides.pivot: If a student will not finish by minute 40, record catch-up and allow a teacher-sample reflection start.

texts: Use Find out why Before You Reflect

Find out why
Which interest raised or lowered this match?
What part fits or surprises you?

A result can be useful even when you dislike it.
slides.lookFor: Final lap: each finished student opens one career and Find out why.
slides.pivot: Use the teacher-sample result for students whose assessment is still pending.

texts:
Use today’s reflection page.

1. What result surprised you, and why?
2. What did Find out why show?
3. How did one interest affect a match?
slides.lookFor: All three prompts have a reason or example; students do not post screenshots or public results.
slides.pivot: Use the three sentence frames, speech-to-text, or private conference record.
